decisions.reason: As a consumer superfood product with weaker strategic fit than the firm's industrial circular-economy technologies, it is the most likely candidate to be discontinued so resources can be redirected to core ventures.

These modular waste-to-energy extensions fit the firm's established engineering and decentralized energy offer, so management would likely retain them even if they are marketed more as add-ons than as a flagship standalone product.
The waste-oil-to-energy plant is strongly aligned with the firm's core waste-to-energy business and was presented prominently, making it likely to stay on the market.

Plastic-waste-to-fuel is a strategic adjacent technology with some commercialization and regulatory risk, but it is close enough to the firm's core sustainability platform that management would probably continue it for now.
